articles.title: Marcos' satisfaction rating falls to -11 -- SWS survey
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr."s satisfaction rating fell to -11, according to a recent survey conducted by the Social Weather Stations (SWS).

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 7:17pm
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s satisfaction rating fell to -11 points, according to a recent survey conducted by the Social Weather Stations (SWS).

In its latest survey released on Thursday, the SWS found that as of September 2026, around 35% of Filipino adults were satisfied with Marcos’ performance, 20% were undecided and 46% were dissatisfied.

Put together, this resulted in a net satisfaction score of -11, which the polling firm designated as “poor”. This is a four point decline from his -7 rating in June, which the SWS labeled as “neutral”.
However, this latest score remains higher than Marcos’ record low score of -15 in March 2026.

Marcos’ net satisfaction rating was the highest in Balance Luzon at neutral net zero, followed by a poor rating of -13 in Visayas, a poor waiting of -21 in Mindanao, and another poor rating of -27 in Metro Manila.

In all areas except Mindanao, Marcos’ satisfaction ratings fell from his June 2026 survey results. His satisfaction ratings in Balance Luzon fell by 11 points from +11, 10 points from -3 in Visayas, three points from -24 in Metro Manila.
Marcos’ net satisfaction ratings in Mindanao eased however, rising by 14 points from -35 in June.

The survey was conducted from September 21 to 27, using face to face interviews with 1,500 adults. A total of 600 of them came from Balance Luzon or Luzon areas outside of Metro Manila, while 300 respondents each came from Metro Manila, Visayas and Mindanao.
There was a sampling error of ±3% for national percentages, ±4% for Balance Luzon, and ±6% each for Metro Manila, the Visayas, and Mindanao.
SONA reception

The survey also asked respondents about Marcos’ penultimate State of the Nation Address (SONA). It said around 47% of Filipinos have heard of Marcos’ SONA, with most of them getting their information from social media.
The SWS said that 53% of Filipinos did not hear or read about the SONA.

Among those who did watch the SONA, 27% watched the address on Facebook and other websites, 15% heard about it on television, 12% watched it live on television, 4% heard about it from other people, 3% listened to stories about it on the radio, 1% listened to the SONA live on the radio, listened to it live on the radio, and 0.4% read about it on newspapers.
Those who watched the SONA were also asked how believable they found Marcos’ speech to be.

From this group, only 13% said that Marcos’ speech was all believable, and another 13% said that it was more believable than unbelievable. Meanwhile, 37% said that the believable and unbelievable were equal.
Around 22% said that the speech was more unbelievable than believable, and 15% said that it was all unbelievable.
Put together, this was equal to a net believability score of -11. This was down by -8 from his speech’s score of -3 in September 2025.
The SWS found that Marcos’ net satisfaction rating was the same whether or not the respondents listened to the SONA. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Witness: VP Sara received compensation from Davao City gov't in 2023
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte received compensation income from the Davao City government in 2023, a witness from the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) said Thursday.

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 7:15pm
Vice President Sara Duterte received compensation income from the Davao City government in 2023, a witness from the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) said Thursday.

Lawyer Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez, the chief of staff of BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza, made the testimony during Day 36 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President, at which was presented BIR Form 2316 or the annual income and tax report of the Vice President for year 2023.

“The BIR Form 2316 is a certificate issued by an employer to an employee. This also states how much is the income that the employer gave to the employee and states the withheld tax of the employer to the BIR. Based on this form, the employer’s name [of the Vice President] is the city government of Davao,” said Garcia-Marquez said.

Asked if the said form was signed by individuals and by whom, the BIR official said yes and added that it was signed by "the city accountant of the City Government of Davao, Ms. Vengeline Bahan, at ang employee po ay si VP Sara Duterte po.”
(The employee here is the Vice President).

Asked by private prosecutor Erwin Matib what such documents mean, Garcia-Marquez replied, “Ang ibig sabihin po ay naka-receive po si VP Sara Duterte ng compensation income from the city government of Davao ng taxable year 2023 po.”
(This means the Vice President received a compensation income from the city government of Davao for the taxable year 2023.)

Matib proceeded to ask the BIR official about the reason for Duterte receiving compensation from Davao City while she is Vice President, but defense counsel Kristine Ferrer objected on the ground of incompetence of the witness.
Matib moved on by asking the witness to read Constitutional provisions stating the prohibition on such an act.
These include:

items: Section 13, Article 7 which states that “the President, Vice President, the members of the cabinet and their deputies or assistants shall not, unless otherwise provided in this Constitution hold any other office or employment during their tenure” and that “they shall not during said tenure directly or indirectly practice any other profession, participate in any business or be financially interested in any contract with or in any franchise or special privilege granted by the government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries” and
Section 6, Article 7 which states that the President and Vice-President “shall not receive during their tenure any other emolument from the Government or any other source.”

blocks.text: The prosecution is presenting evidence to prove Article 2 of the impeachment case against the Vice President amassed unexplained wealth due to alleged failure to truthfully disclose assets in her SALN and failure to divest in businesses as required for the President and Vice President under a Constitutional provision. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Nobel Prize in Literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
articles.summary: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her deep reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

image.caption: Anne Carson has been touted amongst the favorites to win the prize for several years [FILE: 2015]Image: Pontus Lundahl/TT/IMAGO

blocks.text: The Swedish Academy awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in literature to Anne Carson on Thursday, praising her "bold and inventive oeuvre."
Her work has "in playful dialogue with the classical tradition...created new forms for contemporary literature," said Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the academy.

The 76-year-old writer is a longtime professor of classics, creative writing, and comparative literature at prestigious institutions like McGill and Princeton universities. She is only the 19th woman of 123 laureates to win the award.
What is Anne Carson known for?
Born in Toronto in 1950, her family moved around many small towns in Canada during her youth. She has credited a beloved Latin teacher for sparking her interest in language and classics.

Her first book of criticism, 1986’s Eros the Bittersweet, was published to great acclaim and has had significant influence on other classicists, poets, and even film and television. Carson has also published her own poetry such as the 2001 collection The Beauty of the Husband as well as highly regard translation of ancient Greek poets such as Sappho and Sophocles.

Carson is also highly influenced by the King James Bible, as well as more modern writers like Emily Dickinson and Virginia Woolf. She has received numerous awards such as the T.S. Eliot Prize for Poetry, a MacArthur fellowship, and the PEN/Nabokov award.

Deeply private, Carson often declines to speak about her personal life in interviews and discourages autobiographical interpretations of her work. However, she did reveal in 2024 that she suffers from Parkinson's disease.
Who else has received a Nobel Prize so far?

items: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their pioneering work on optogenetics, a method of controlling nerve cells with light, which makes it possible to study how the brain works.
The Nobel Prize in physics was awarded Tuesday to Francis Halzen, a Belgian-born astrophysicist whose efforts helped demistify a rare group of neutrinos that launched a new era of astronomy.
The Nobel Prize in chemistry went to Henri B. Kagan of France and Kenso Soai of Japan on Wednesday, for solving the longstanding mystery of homochirality in living organisms.

blocks.text: What happens next?

The winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature receives prize money of 12 million Swedish kronor, equivalent to about $1.2 million. They are also given a medal and a diploma at an official ceremony in December, where they are expected to deliver a speech known as a Nobel lecture.
On Friday, the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize will be announced, following by the Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel on Monday.

articles.title: US infant defies bleak odds from rare congenital trait: ‘Don’t quit before your child quits’
articles.summary:
Wren Michelle Roberts was born with heterotaxy, a syndrome so rare a specialist could only find 15 similar cases

South-eastern

blocks.text: South-eastern Louisiana couple Nick and Savannah Roberts planned to bury their infant daughter the weekend after she was born in September with an exceedingly rare combination of birth defects that her doctors feared was unsurvivable.

But an unforeseen congenital trait in Wren Michelle Roberts’ heart, combined with her parents’ dedication to her complex medical care, has allowed her to defy her bleak initial prognosis and meet weeks’ worth of milestones that each are a “miracle in [their] own way”, according to her doctor.

As the one-month mark since her birth approached on Wednesday, Wren’s parents said they had been able to bring her to a high school football game, introducing her to one of their region’s timeless fall traditions. The Robertses, residents of the suburban New Orleans community of Montz, said they had also been able to bring their daughter to church.

Wren is immunocompromised, and those outings saw the family observe myriad protective measures, from minimizing close contact with people outside their household to keeping a plastic covering over her bassinet, Nick said.
Nonetheless, Nick said he, his wife and their supporters savored each activity as much as they did on the first occasions that Wren drank a bottle, took a pacifier, cried and cooed.
“This is awesome,” Nick said. “Like this is just normal stuff – and she’s doing what she’s supposed to be doing, going with the flow.”

Wren was born with what is known as heterotaxy syndrome, according to her physician, Dr Gabriella Bluett-Mills of New Orleans’ Ochsner Children’s Hospital. Generally, the organs of those with that congenital condition do not form in the positions that they should, Bluett-Mills said.
And in Wren’s case, she was born with her stomach in her chest, no spleen to help fight infections, spina bifida and multiple heart defects.

Bluett-Mills, a pediatric complex care specialist, said she and her team could only find 15 documented examples – across the whole of medical literature – of cases involving the same specific genetic mutation at the center of Wren’s case.

The Robertses first realized Wren would be like few other babies after testing done 20 weeks into Savannah’s pregnancy. Nick, a chemical plant employee, recalled doctors advising him and Savannah, a nurse, to prepare for the reality that Wren would probably die before her birth given the substantial complications surrounding her syndrome.
That prompted the Robertses to go so far as to plan for a funeral days after she was born.

Yet Wren ultimately was able to outlive the worst case scenario. And Bluett-Mills said all indications are that is because an abnormal blood vessel in Wren’s heart had attributed which turned out to be fortuitous in her case.

Among the reasons the kind of vessel in question – known as a major aortopulmonary collateral artery, or Mapca – is problematic is that in many cases it is obstructed. But in Wren’s case it is not obstructed, her father said, citing what physicians have told him.

Bluett-Mills furthermore said doctors have been able to determine that all of the blood from Wren’s heart is going into that one vessel before splitting off – with some going to her body to give her more oxygen and the rest going to her lungs to get more oxygen put into it.
“Without that particular setup – if one of those two things wasn’t happening – she would not be alive,” Bluett-Mills said.

Not all of the milestones which that vessel has set the stage for have been as celebratory for Wren as going to mass or an evening under the lights of a Friday night high school football game for the first time.

She had spinal surgery at one week old. And Bluett-Mills said there are more doctors’ appointments in her future than is likely going to be typical for most of the babies around Wren, who stays nourished with the help of a feeding tube.

But the Ochsner pediatric complex care specialist said Wren’s progress in her infancy has reminded her of physicians’ “need to look at the patient in front of us who is telling us that she is very much alive and wants to kind of hit some of these milestones, do these things that no one was expecting her to do, and we have to watch the baby in front of us to make the decision about what to do next.”
“Every one of her milestones is something … all of us are celebrating as … its own miracle in its own way,” Bluett-Mills said.

Meanwhile, Nick and Savannah Roberts have been documenting their and their daughter’s emotional journey on a Facebook page named Wren’s Warriors. The page had amassed a following of nearly 8,000 users which Wren’s parents say have rallied around their family as their baby grows.
Nick told the Guardian he had already derived a poignant lesson on fatherhood from Wren: “Don’t quit [before] your child quits. … If they’re not giving up, then you can’t give up.”

Savannah spoke to local news outlet WVUE about how her perspective as a nurse made it particularly difficult for her to learn that her pregnancy had complications. But she told the outlet that Wren inspired her to believe in the extraordinary.
“You’re still fighting, you’re still here,” Wren’s mother later wrote to her daughter in a Facebook post. “Keep fighting, sweet girl.”

articles.title: Mark Villar switches camps. Minutes later, family’s troubled firms make their move.
articles.summary: It’s been a busy afternoon for the Villars, as Mark crosses to the Senate majority, Camille stays, and three of the family's suspended firms move to finally release their long-overdue financial…

blocks.text: It’s been a busy afternoon for the Villars, as Mark crosses to the Senate majority, Camille stays, and three of the family's suspended firms move to finally release their long-overdue financial statements

items: Senator Mark Villar switched to the majority in the Senate, gaining the public works committee chairmanship, while his sister remained in the minority, allowing the Villar family to maintain influence in both political camps.

Shortly after Villar's political maneuver, three companies under the Villar umbrella announced plans to release their overdue audited financial statements, raising speculation about their potential return to trading on the Philippine Stock Exchange after months of suspension.

The Villar family's financial troubles are significant, with multiple companies facing scrutiny and legal issues, including a major controversy involving Villar Land Holdings, which reported inflated asset values and is under investigation for various violations.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
A Villar switches political camps, and seemingly on cue, parts of the family’s battered business empire stir to life.

On Thursday, October 8 – amid an extended lunch break in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, and with the Senate about to go on a month-long legislative recess – there was apparently just enough time for Senator Mark Villar to switch to the majority and promptly snag the powerful public works committee chairmanship and a seat in the Commission on Appointments. His sister, Senator Camille Villar, stayed put in the minority, leaving the family a foot in both camps.

Minutes later came the corporate disclosures. Between 2:12 pm and 3:09 pm, three companies under the Villar family’s corporate umbrella announced moves that could bring them closer to resuming trading on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE), following months of suspension and controversy.
Talk about timing.

In separate, successive PSE disclosures, Vista Land & Lifescapes (VLL), Vistamalls (STR), and VistaREIT (VREIT) announced that their boards had approved the release of their long-overdue audited financial statements for 2025.

Coming just minutes after news of Villar’s flip in the Senate broke, the filings were enough to set tongues wagging in stock market analyst circles, with speculation about the family’s political maneuvering and whether its suspended companies might finally be inching toward a return to stock market trading.

But the three companies are only part of a bigger mess nagging at the Villars. In all, six of the family’s listed companies have been pushed out of stock market trading after repeatedly missing financial reporting deadlines. First came their overdue 2025 annual reports, then their Q1 2026 financial statements, followed by their Q2 reports. For months, investors have been left holding shares they cannot sell.

Thursday’s announcements are also far from enough to get the stocks trading again. The three companies have merely authorized the release of their 2025 audited statements, which have yet to be published on the exchange. There’s no word on their overdue quarterly reports either.
And that’s just three of the six. AllHome (HOME), AllDay Marts (ALLDY), and, most notably, Villar Land Holdings (VLC) made no similar announcements.

blocks.caption: Anyare? Villars’ AllHome, AllDay confirm store closures

blocks.text: The last of these is particularly conspicuous. Villar Land Holdings is at the center of the family’s biggest financial controversy, after initially reporting a staggering P1.3 trillion in assets for 2024, driven by an unbelievable revaluation of its properties in Villar City.
Its subsequently audited statements showed assets of only P35.7 billion, a fraction of the earlier figure.
Since then, it has been one controversy after another for the Villar family. Among their mounting troubles:

items: In August 2025, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) fined Villar Land and its directors and officers P12 million over reporting violations. Months later, it revoked property appraiser E-Value Phils.’ accreditation and fined it P1 million over unreliable valuations.

In January 2026, the SEC filed a criminal complaint against Villar Land, family members, and related firms over alleged market manipulation, insider trading, and misleading disclosures. The Villars have denied wrongdoing and sought its dismissal.

In September, the Ombudsman filed graft and administrative complaints against the Villar family over its PrimeWater contracts with local water districts. In San Jose del Monte, Bulacan, a water crisis affecting over 47,000 households prompted a state of calamity and the city government’s takeover of PrimeWater’s operations, with Metro Pacific Water brought in as interim operator.
Before trading was suspended, Villar Land shares last traded at P448 as of May 29, a drop off the cliff from their 52-week high of P2,300.

blocks.text: Francis Lim, the man tasked with keeping watch over the country’s corporations, has made clear that even the most powerful families are not untouchable.

blocks.caption: SEC chief Francis Lim to Villars: No family is too powerful to sue

blocks.text: “If you deserve to be sued, we will sue you,” the SEC chairman said in July, referring to the case against the Villars. The SEC’s criminal complaint remains under preliminary investigation at the Department of Justice.
Time will tell whether Mark Villar’s moves will be enough to build back the fallen family’s political and financial capital. – Rappler.com

articles.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
articles.summary: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not…

image.caption: The dispute can trace its roots back to President Zelenskyy's speech at the UN General Assembly last month [FILE: September 23, 2026]Image: Seth Wenig/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: South Korea said on Thursday that it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine amid a deepening diplomatic rift over making the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul public last month.

The two countries have been at loggerheads since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's speech at the UN General Assembly, during which he spoke about the capture and later the transfer of two North Korean soldiers who had been fighting against Ukraine alongside Russian forces.
South Korea has called for an apology from Ukraine, saying the comments breached a confidentiality agreement and could put the POWs' families still in North Korea at risk.
Kyiv, meanwhile, has said no such agreement existed and voiced a desire to smooth over a "diplomatic understanding," but stopped short of apologizing.

blocks.caption: A South Korean lawmaker, Yu Yong-weon, had visited the POWs at a camp in Ukraine after their captureImage: Kim Hong-Ji/REUTERS

blocks.text: What did South Korea's Foreign Ministry say about recalling its ambassador?
"The govenment has decided to recall its ambassador to Ukraine," Seoul's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.
"The government hopes that all outstanding issues between the two countries will be resolved amicably and wil continue consultations with the Ukrainian side to that end," it said.

blocks.caption: North Korea's Kim Jong Un has posed prominently with wounded soldiers who were deployed to assist Russian in its war against UkraineImage: KCNA/KNS/AFP

blocks.text: Last week, President Lee Jae Myung called for a "public apology" from Kyiv and said South Korea would take "additional measures" if one was not forthcoming. He said that during the prisoner swap, "the Ukrainian side demanded confidentiality and agreed to it, but unilaterally disclosed it."

When challenged with what Myung described as "utmost courtesy," he said Kyiv instead denied the existence of a confidentiality agreement, making him out to be a liar, and spoke of the prospect of war on the Korean peninsula.
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, meanwhile, had spoken of a "diplomatic misunderstanding" that he said "we sincerely hope to resolve."
Why Seoul wants an apology from Zelenskyy

Bilateral tensions also emerged this week amid the publication of an investigative report in The Guardian claiming that fuel was being shipped to Russia from South Korea via sanctioned tankers, alleviating the strains on diesel supplies amid Ukraine targeting Russian refineries and other oil infrastructure.

South Korea has walked a fine line on Russia's war in Ukraine, providing humanitarian and non-lethal equipment to Kyiv, as well as financial assistance, but also seeking to maintain cordial ties with Russia, which has a small land border with North Korea near Vladivostock.

North Korea, meanwhile, sent troops to help Russia reclaim the border region of Kursk that Ukraine was able to partially occupy, and has since celebrated this deployment at home with much fanfare, while seeking closer ties to Putin's Russia.

blocks.caption: North Korea has elected to use the deployment in Russia as a tool for domestic propaganda and diplomatic relations rather than to keep it quietImage: KCNA/REUTERS

articles.title: As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
articles.summary: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

image.caption: Data centers are essential for maintaining online servicesImage: Serjunco/Westend61/IMAGO

blocks.text: Hackers and power outages were once the largest threat to Ukraine's data centers. Now, it is the buildings themselves that are in the cross hairs.
Since early September, Russia has been targeting these centers, which house the physical infrastructure needed to store digital information, systematically.

Digital infrastructure in and around the capital Kyiv was already affected but after the attacks, several television channels and streaming services were temporarily unavailable. Subscribers to several cable networks also reported that they had difficulties connecting.
Why is Russia targeting Ukrainian data centers?

The servers and computer systems needed to store data and keep online services operating smoothly are a crucial target because if they are damaged, it can have a nationwide effect. All online systems, ranging from news portals, state registries, banking and finance, need functioning data centers to operate smoothly.

Ukrainian Minister of Foreign Affairs Andrii Sybiha said Russia had targeted major Ukrainian data centers to disrupt the flow of information. "As Russia isn’t achieving its goals on the battlefield, it is seeking new ways to destabilize life in Ukraine and terrorize civilians."
Has Russia changed its approach in its war with Ukraine?
Could Ukraine go offline?

Despite widespread damage caused by Russian attacks, experts do not believe the country risks having a complete internet blackout. Telecommunications expert Oleksandr Glushchenko told DW that this was because the entire sector was quite decentralized.

"The industry was never regulated in Ukraine, and no multi-million licenses were required,” he explained. "Entering the market was very affordable, which is why thousands of businesses started offering their services."

He added that Ukrainians could choose between multiple providers — and in some cases up to 10. This competition, he said, meant that Ukraine had "some of the best internet provider services in the world."
At the same time, he noted, damage caused by kinetic attacks could cause certain providers to "go dark" while repairs took place.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian lawmaker Oleksandr Fediienko, who is a member of the parliamentary Committee on National Security, Defense and Intelligence, posted similar sentiments on the social network Facebook: "Will the internet disappear in Ukraine? Of course not. The infrastructure will be restructured, and alternative sites will be established." He added that the Russian attacks made no sense because Ukrainian providers were able to restore service so quickly.
Lessons from Latvia: How to deal with Russian hybrid threats

Serhii Beskrestnov, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's advisor on defense technology, said that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian data centers were part of a wider campaign. "They've already been scaring us with claims that there won't be food or fuel, and now they're scaring us with the prospect of losing internet access," he wrote on Facebook.
How can data and devices be protected?

Glushchenko said that even if a server was destroyed, its data would be available from other data centers where it was stored, including abroad. "The system can automatically switch to a different data center," he explained.
He pointed out that telecommunications companies also stored copies with cloud services offered by providers such as Google and Amazon.
What happens when data centers lose power?

Oleksandr Olshanskyi, the founder of the Ukrainian web hosting provider MiroHost and also the head of the leading Ukrainian IT service company Internet Invest, told the Ukrainian news agency RBC-Ukraine that his data center had been almost totally destroyed but that this had not made a major difference. He said that the vast majority of his clients remained unaffected, as they could fall back on operation capacities in Poland and the Czech Republic. "I'm only left with about 150 out of 20,000 to 25,000 clients, who for some reason did not shift, duplicate or secure their data," he explained.

Tech experts have recommended that Ukrainian data centers place a higher priority on decentralization, saying they should be as spread out as possible geographically, and also that data should be cloned and secured in other data centers abroad. Moving infrastructure into underground spaces could also be a solution, but this would translate into extra costs for customers.
"We've grown accustomed to having the fastest and cheapest internet in Europe, and the best technical support," Fediienko said but pointed out that this was "about to change."
Beskrestnov also expected the price of internet services to rise soon, to cover the costs of repairing damage to infrastructure.
This article was originally published in Ukrainian.

articles.title: Asos says customer data accessed by hacker posing as trusted contact
articles.summary: Customers are told payment details and passwords were not compromised when employee account was breached

blocks.text: Hackers gained access to Asos customer names and contact details by impersonating a “trusted contact” to gain access to one of its employee’s accounts, the retailer has said.
Thousands of users of the online fashion seller’s app received a notification on Tuesday titled “Asos hacked” with a link to the Telegram messaging service, sending its shares diving by about 10%.

After carrying out a “detailed, 48-hour investigation” into the incident Asos confirmed that basic personal information of customers, including names and contact details, had been accessed by an unidentified third party.
Asos said the group had also gained access to “certain non-personal account related information”, without clarifying what this was. Payment card details or passwords had not been accessed, it added.

The retailer said in a message to customers on Thursday: “We discovered that an unauthorised party gained access to an Asos employee account by impersonating a trusted contact to obtain login credentials. Those credentials were then used to access information on certain third-party platforms used by Asos.

“The affected platforms were immediately locked down, ensuring that no further information could be accessed, and a full investigation was launched with the support of both internal and external cyber experts. We are also working with the relevant law enforcement and regulatory authorities.”
It said the Asos website and app continued to be safe to use and customers did not need to take action and added that it had “already taken additional steps to further strengthen security controls”.

However, the company warned: “Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos. We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call.”
Asos pledged to contact customers directly once its investigation was complete and “where we believe additional information, support or action may be required”.
after newsletter promotion

The Telegram channel operated by the purported hackers, who have named themselves the Xuanye Group, that users were directed to on Tuesday carried a message assuring Asos customers that “payment information is not affected”.
Cyber experts said that they had not heard of the group before and that the push notification could be an attempt to gain wider attention.

articles.title: Queensland literary awards: ‘stunning’ debut inspired by segregated shantytown wins top prize
articles.summary:
Lenora Thaker wins $30,000 prize for ‘a work of state significance’ for The Pearl of Tagai Town, which draws on her family’s history in Cairns-Malay Town

A “stunning” debut novel described…

blocks.text: A “stunning” debut novel described as “unambiguously and distinctively Queensland” has won the $30,000 top prize at the Queensland literary awards (QLAs).

blocks.caption: The Pearl of Tagai Town by Lenora Thaker. Photograph: Text Publishing

blocks.text: Meriam and Wagedagam author Lenora Thaker won the Queensland premier’s award for a work of state significance for her historical novel The Pearl of Tagai Town, which was inspired by her ancestors’ lives in an unmapped shantytown known as Cairns-Malay Town. The town once housed Indigenous Australians, Chinese, Indian, Japanese, Malaysian and Sri Lankan residents who had been segregated from the white population; it existed from the late 1800s until the late 1950s.
The QLA judges praised Thaker’s “accessible and deeply enjoyable” book for its “vivid sense of place”.

“Warm, richly drawn characters and an innovative integration of Ailan languages come together in a rich, cohesive whole, bringing new insight and fresh imaginative life to a far north Queensland community. The Pearl of Tagai Town is a stunning debut novel,” the judges wrote in a joint statement.
The winners were announced at a ceremony on Thursday night at Brisbane Powerhouse, as part of Brisbane writers festival.

Claire Thomas won the $15,000 fiction category for On Not Climbing Mountains, which follows a woman on a trip in Switzerland, who distracts herself from grief with research on famous names who had connections to the country.

The $15,000 nonfiction prize went to Find Me at the Jaffa Gate: An Encyclopaedia of a Palestinian Family by Australian-Palestinian writer Micaela Sahhar, about how her family’s story was shaped by the Nakba, when more than 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled from their homes by Israel during the country’s founding in 1948. Sahhar won the same category at the Victorian premier’s literary awards in February.

The $15,000 children’s book category was won by Once I Was a Giant by Zeno Sworder, which has also won book of the year at the Australian Book Industry awards and the children’s category at the Victorian premier’s literary award. Illustrated and written by Sworder, the book tells the tale of a tree transformed into a pencil that then writes its own story.

Julianne Negri won the $15,000 young adult category for her book The Belly of a Wolf, Helena Pantsis won the $15,000 short story category for her collection Mother Salad, and Eunice Andrada won the $17,500 poetry category for her collection Kontra.

The $15,000 people’s choice category was won by Sita Walker’s debut In a Common Hour, a novel that takes place across a single hour at a state high school. Walker has been a teacher for more than 20 years, and currently teaches English at a high school in Brisbane’s south-east.

Founded in 1999, the QLAs were previously known as the Queensland premier’s literary awards until 2012, when they were abolished by then premier Campbell Newman. Queensland’s literary community intervened to keep the awards alive.

The QLAs were administered by the State Library of Queensland from 2014 until 2025, when the awards were embroiled in controversy over the arts minister John-Paul Langbroek’s intervention to stop the library awarding a $15,000 fellowship to First Nations author K A Ren Wyld, over a social media post about the dead Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar.
Wyld said she had posted the comment in an “emotional moment”, and that her winning manuscript had nothing to do with Gaza.

Twelve QLA judges resigned in protest of Wyld’s treatment, leading to last year’s awards being delayed. Langbroek eventually handed their management over to the Brisbane writers festival from this year.

articles.title: Ukraine says 30 killed, 18 wounded in Russian attack on passenger buses in Kramatorsk
articles.summary: Authorities in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk have suspended public transport following the deadly attack near the front line.

image.caption: A bus burns following a Russian airstrike in Kramatorsk, where Ukrainian authorities say at least 30 people were killed in an attack on passenger busesImage: National Police of Ukraine/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: A Russian strike on two passenger buses in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk has killed at least 30 people and wounded 18 others, authorities said on Thursday.
The Donetsk regional prosecutor's office confirmed the death toll following the attack on Telegram on Thursday morning.
What do we know about the attack?
The regional governor's office reported the same figures and said public transport services had been suspended.
Governor Vadym Filashkin said Russian forces were deliberately targeting civilian transport.
"For them, a bus with passengers is an attractive target precisely because one strike can kill as many people as possible," he said.
"Russia deliberately disregards all conceivable rules of warfare and the norms of international humanitarian law," he said. "It chooses targets where it can cause the most pain to civilians."
Has Russia changed its approach in its war with Ukraine?
"Under such circumstances, we have no right to risk the lives of passengers and drivers," he said. "The safety of the residents of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk is now above all else."
Earlier reports had put the death toll at 12, with 14 wounded.
Why is Kramatorsk strategically important?
Kramatorsk lies close to the front line in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. It is one of the main Ukrainian-held cities in the Donetsk region, which Russia claims to have annexed.
The city has served as a key military logistics hub throughout much of the war and forms part of Ukraine's heavily defended eastern "fortress belt."
Russian forces have advanced toward the city's eastern outskirts, prompting calls for remaining civilians to evacuate to safer areas.

articles.title: In just 4 years, Marcos tops 2 predecessors in foreign travel budget, number of trips
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has already made 47 foreign trips, surpassing president Benigno Aquino III and Rodrigo Duterte’s number of trips.

items: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is on a working visit to Singapore from October 7 to 11, marking his sixth trip to the country and bringing his total international trips to 47 during his presidency.

Marcos has surpassed his two predecessors in terms of travel frequency and budget, with a significant focus on strengthening foreign relations and promoting the Philippines as an investment destination.

His trips include various types of visits, with 27 being working visits, and he has received increased budget allocations for foreign travel, reflecting his administration's commitment to international engagement.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. will see the skies once again on a working visit to Singapore from October 7 to 11.
He may yet be the country’s most traveled president in more than a decade.

His itinerary to the Lion City includes a meeting with Prime Minister and finance chief Lawrence Wong, the 24th Forbes Global CEO Conference, a visit to the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute, and watching the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix.
This is now his sixth visit to Singapore, his second to the country in 2026. This is also his third time off to the race tracks watching the Formula 1 Grand Prix.
In just his first four years in office, this brings his total international trips to 47, eclipsing his two immediate predecessors, former presidents Benigno Aquino III and Rodrigo Duterte.
Both former presidents were known to have an aversion to foreign travel, especially long-distance trips.
Marcos, who was 64 when he became President, has already surpassed Duterte in international travel budget and is poised to exceed the two past presidents in terms of spending.

Duterte, who was in his early to mid-70s during his presidency, had been vocal about hating traveling overseas. His foreign travel was also limited by COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, with some multilateral meetings shifting online.
Aquino, who was in his early 50s, also hated long trips because he couldn’t stand being without cigarettes for hours.
Presidential foreign trips help strengthen a country’s foreign relations. These trips may also include discussions on the country’s defense, economy, and investments.
The President’s International Travels

Manila (MNL) ➔ Indonesia
September 4–6, 2022 • State Visit
Trade talks, Defense talks, meeting Filipino communities
Marcos made his first overseas trip in his third month in office. He had seven in his first six months.
The President had the most in 2023 and 2024 at 12 each. In 2025, he slowed down to eight despite receiving the biggest allocation so far. For 2026, Marcos has had eight.
The President has been vocal in his commitment to promoting the country as an investment destination to other nations.
But University of the Philippines Diliman Department of Political Science Professor Jean S. Encinas-Franco said the increase may also be a part of Marcos’ plan to rehabilitate his family’s name.
She added that it may also be a way to diversify foreign allies amid rising tensions in the West Philippine Sea.

“The Marcos administration has decided to engage more with the international community to show that the Philippine government has support from other countries. And also to show that Marcos is trying to diversify the country’s allies,” said Franco.
She also said that the trips will help make the country more visible on the global stage.
“The perception that the Philippines is out there in the world, has many allies, will always show up, or that we are always advocating for our causes or the global agenda,” said Encinas-Franco.
“It’s also important that they get to talk to their potential partners. The government gets to introduce private sector companies who are sometimes part of this delegation,” she added.
The President takes on different types of presidential trips. These vary depending on the level of formality and ceremony. (READ: Presidential trips: What you need to know)

State visits are the highest form of diplomatic visits, with grand ceremonies and meals that honor the relations of the two countries. Official visits, on the other hand, have less grandeur, and a state lunch or dinner is optional. They usually have a smaller delegation.
Lastly, working visits are trips meant for meeting with other government officials to tackle issues that concern bilateral relations.
Expenses in state and official visits are usually covered by the host country. Meanwhile, the Office of the President (OP) pays for expenses during working visits.
Frequency of Presidential Visits by Type

Official Classification Frequency & Share
Source: Official Gazette, Presidential Communications Office
So far, 27 of Marcos’ visits are official working visits for international summits and conferences. He also has had 12 state visits and seven official visits during his presidency.

Marcos had an “unofficial trip” to Singapore from September 30 to October 2, 2022. During the trip, he attended business meetings and talked about investments in the country. On the same trip, he was also spotted watching the Formula One (F1) Singapore Grand Prix.
Former executive secretary Lucas Bersamin clarified that the trip was “semi-official.”

Singapore appears to be among the President’s favorites, with six visits. This ties with the United States as his most frequent destination; two were official visits while the rest were working visits.

He visited Washington DC three times to meet with the US president and attend meetings, and once in San Francisco for the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. He has also been to New York twice, where their family lived for some time during their exile and where he met First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos.
Marcos also visited Indonesia four times, and Japan and Malaysia three times each. These five countries alone account for 46.9% of the President’s reported trips.
Encinas-Franco said that most of the time, the US hosts the larger summits and United Nations general assemblies, which contribute to the recurring trips by the administration.
Since his administration’s first year crafting the budget, the OP’s foreign travel expenses have dwarfed their local counterparts.

*Values in Philippine Pesos (PHP)

In 2025, Marcos received his biggest travel allocation so far at P1.7 billion — P1.6 billion was allotted for foreign trips. In the same year, his office benefited from a P720-million increase in the proposed P913.96 billion National Expenditure Program.
The President’s 2026 travel budget also received an additional P6 million.
Encinas-Franco explained that the additional funding granted may be due to the President’s increased international appearances.

Marcos has already surpassed Duterte in terms of foreign travel budget allocations, based on the General Appropriations Act (GAA) from 2023 to 2026. The President received P3.74 billion from 2023 to 2026, compared to Duterte’s P2.55-billion total allocations for the same period.
Meanwhile, Aquino’s appropriations for his international trips were included in the office’s contingent funds.
Foreign travel expenses comprise the total cost incurred by an individual or office when traveling to other countries for official business meetings, work assignments, and government duties.

Each government agency must fund its own travel expenses from its allocated budget, according to Executive Order No. 77 and Memorandum Circular No. 50. Spending should be cost-effective and not excessive, and foreign travel must meet the agency’s needs and benefit the country.
While there is no official limit for the presidential delegation, the two guidelines require the person’s presence to be critical to the trip’s outcome.
For presidential trips, a cap of two officials per agency is set. Private individuals, spouses or children of officials, and consultants are not covered by government expenses.
During these trips, agencies must allocate funds for pre-departure expenses, daily subsistence allowance, accommodations (room sharing is mandated if possible), and clothing for their delegates.
These agencies declare their actual spending within a period in the financial statements submitted to the Commission on Audit (COA), which is included in the commission’s Annual Audit Report.
Based on these statements, Marcos is on pace to eclipse the two previous presidents in terms of spending.

In 2022, the President exceeded the P201-million budget allotted for foreign trips, spending P396 million. Duterte, who crafted that year’s budget, made no foreign trips in his last six months in office.

However, the president can realign expenses. Article VI, Section 25 of the Constitution states that the president may transfer leftover funds within his or her own office from one line item to another.
COA has already flagged the Marcos administration for over P14.4 million in unsettled funds for foreign travel from 2022 to 2024, covering hotel accommodations and airfare for various agencies.
In 2025, Malacañang said that the office has recovered 55% of the unsettled funds from concerned government agencies. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Russia health officials deny reports of 2nd plague death in Siberia
articles.summary: Russia's health regulator said ‌Thursday that reports that a ​second person had ​fallen ill following the death ​of a worker at ‌a plague research laboratory in Siberia were false.

blocks.text: Health·New
Russia's health regulator said ‌Thursday that reports that a ​second person had ​fallen ill following the death ​of a worker at ‌a plague research laboratory in Siberia were false.
World Health Organization estimates public risk of Russia case to be low, based on what has been made known
WHO investigates second pneumonia case linked to Russian anti-plague lab
Russia's health regulator said ‌Thursday that reports that a ​second person had ​fallen ill following the death ​of a ⁠worker ⁠at ‌a plague research laboratory in Siberia were false.

Preventive ⁠measures have been completed for ‌all individuals who had contact with the first worker ​who ⁠died last week, ⁠and no dangerous ⁠pathogenic ⁠microorganisms ​have been detected, said ​the Russia health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor.

Russian authorities have said 28-year-old Daria Shipilova died last Friday ‌from pneumonia of an as-yet-unestablished origin. Shipilova was a lab employee at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far ‌East, located in the town of Shelekhov, prompting authorities in Russia to swiftly roll out a series of precautionary anti-epidemic measures that caught global attention.

Rospotrebnadzor said she died of an unknown type of pneumonia ‌and that no relevant pathogens had been found in anyone who came into contact with her. Officials in Russia said she was vaccinated and therefore "immune to the dangerous infections with which she worked."

A security person wearing a face mask looks out from the door of an infectious diseases hospital in the town of Shelekhov, where an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute recently died, a mysterious fatality that has caused international concern. (Tatyana Makeyeva/AFP/Getty Images)

The World Health Organization initially said it ⁠estimated the risk of the Russia case to ⁠the public as low, based on what had been made known, but told a news conference on Wednesday ‌it could not make a fuller risk assessment due to insufficient information from the Russian authorities.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director general of WHO, said the global health body had offered assistance to Russia and also repeated a request to verify "media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause." Those reports started with a Russian media outlet and were spread to English-language audiences by the Daily Mail in Britain, based on a subsequent pneumonia-like death at an Irkutsk hospital.

items: WHO wants more answers from Russia about lab worker's death, as pneumonic plague concerns linger
Did a Russian lab worker die from pneumonic plague? What we know — and don't know

blocks.text: Health Canada has told CBC News it is also monitoring the situation, though it sees no risk to Canada at this time. According to the agency, the last recorded human case of plague in this country was in 1939.

U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Director Erica Schwartz said Wednesday the risk to ‌the U.S. from an unconfirmed pneumonic plague case in Siberia was extremely low, but the agency was prepared to monitor and screen travellers.
What we know about the suspected plague death in Russia

The CDC ‌has a port health station at the John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York that can conduct surveillance and screening for travellers from the region entering the United States, Schwartz said. The U.S. Department ⁠of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether the agency planned to set up screening there.

A spokesperson from Health and Human Services said there are about 200 individuals per year from the Siberian region who travel to the United States. Direct flights between Russia and the United States have been suspended ​since the start of the Ukraine war in 2022.

items: The Philippine Senate ratified the Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA) with France, marking the first such treaty with a European nation.
The SOVFA establishes a legal framework for the presence and activities of the Philippine and French armed forces in each other's territories, facilitating joint defense and humanitarian efforts.
This agreement is part of the Philippines' strategy to expand defense ties amid regional tensions, particularly with China, while also seeking to reset relations with Beijing.

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate on Thursday, October 8, concurred in the ratification of the Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA) between Philippines and France.
With 17 affirmative votes, senators approved proposed Senate Resolution No. 650, concurring in the ratification of the SOVFA, between the two countries.

Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and French Minister for the Armed Forces and Veterans Catherine Vautrin signed the SOVFA in March. The agreement provides a legal framework for the presence and activities of the Philippine and French armed forces in each other’s territories.
“This is a historic moment because this treaty ratification of our visiting forces with France is the first for a European nation,” said Senate Majority Floor Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri
Newly designated French Ambassador to the Philippines Donatienne Hissard personally received the resolution at the Senate.

The SOVFA is a “reciprocal bilateral defense agreement that establishes the legal framework governing the presence and cooperative activities of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the French Armed Forces, including their respective Civilian Components, in each other’s territories, and facilitates joint defense, training, humanitarian, and other mutually agreed activities.”
With the agreement’s ratification, France joins the growing list of countries with visiting forces agreements with the Philippines.

The Philippines has a long-standing Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) with its treaty ally, the United States. In 2012, a SOVFA with Australia, which has since become a strategic partner of the Philippines.

The expansion of the Philippines’ defense ties has been a conscious push of the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. administration, especially in the face of a growingly belligerent China in the South China Sea. At the same time, however, Marcos has said he wants a “reset” of bilateral relations with Beijing, following years of tensions both at sea and in the diplomatic space. – Rappler.com

articles.title: USS Lincoln carrier to return to port in San Diego after record-breaking deployment – US politics live
articles.summary:
Vessel spent over 260 consecutive days at sea without a port call, a US navy record

As Donald Trump struggled to end the war with Iran, and the Lincoln’s deployment dragged on,…

blocks.text: Controversial record-long USS Lincoln deployment over as carrier set to return home to San Diego
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
The USS Abraham Lincoln will return home to San Diego later today after supporting the Iran war during a record long deployment of 265 uninterrupted days at sea.
For months, there have been widespread concerns since reports first emerged of supply shortages and deteriorating mental health onboard.

In remarks yesterday, however, US defense secretary Pete Hegseth sought to play down the issues, instead condemning “a few folks in the media” who he accused of trying to “turn” the Lincoln’s deployment “into some sort of symbol of dysfunction, or a symbol of low morale or a symbol of a failed mission”.

While Trump administration officials pushed back against accounts of poor conditions, families and veterans warned that the length and intensity of the deployment were taking a toll on both those serving onboard and their loved ones.

As reports of conditions leaked out, the Lincoln soon became a flashpoint in the increasingly contentious debate over the war and, for some, a symbol of the strains and pressures the conflict has placed on the US military and the people serving in it.
Hegseth flew out to the carrier on Wednesday to give the crew the Presidential Unit Citation, the highest honor a unit can receive that is typically reserved for significant achievement in combat.
He said that “what makes the US military and the US Navy and all these sailors different is that you adapt and that you’re resilient and you overcome — you finish the mission nonetheless.”
Hegseth told the crew that president Donald Trump “tracked your activities from day one and couldn’t be more proud of what you executed.”

The US carrier, with roughly 5,000 sailors and marines onboard, left San Diego in November 2025, initially bound for the Pacific and expected to return in the spring. But after the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in late February, the Lincoln was redirected to the Middle East, to support US operations in the region.

The Lincoln was relieved from its deployment later in August, as the USS George Washington aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East to take its place.

articles.title: Russian strike on buses kills 33, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
articles.summary: Ukraine accused Russia of targeting the crowded bus in the frontline city to kill as many civilians as possible.

blocks.text: Thirty-three people have been killed in a Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, rescue officials say.
Another 18 people were wounded, said Donetsk regional head Vadym Filashkin, accusing Russia of targeting a bus carrying passengers to kill as many civilians as possible.
Images posted by local prosecutors showed the burning metal shell of the bus along with debris and some of the victims on the road.
Kramatorsk and neighbouring Slovyansk are part of a so-called fortress belt that Russia is trying to seize as part of Vladimir Putin's claim to the entire Ukrainian industrial region of Donbas.
However, Thursday's attack follows a dramatic surge in Russian attacks across the country and a heavy increase in civilian casualties.

Russia is now launching constant air raids against Ukraine, with sirens ringing throughout the day in the capital Kyiv. According to the UN, Ukraine saw more civilians killed by August this year than were killed in all of 2025.

In one single attack that destroyed a five-storey block of flats in Pryluky east of Kyiv early on Wednesday, 22 people were killed, including five children. Three of the children were only one year old.
Moscow is yet to comment on the latest attack, however rescue officials said the attack caused a fire on two buses that were both carrying passengers.
Filashkin appealed to anyone who was still in the Donetsk region to move to safer regions of Ukraine.

Given the sharp deterioration of security in the two neighbouring cities, he said all public transport had been ordered to stop. The safety of civilians was paramount, and "we have no right to risk the lives of passengers and drivers", he said.

Moscow has often cited the "liberation" and "protection" of the predominantly Russian-speaking Donbas as justification for the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. It is made up of two regions - Luhansk and Donetsk - and with most of Luhansk under Russian control, the Kremlin is also aiming to capture remaining 20% of Donetsk territory still held by Ukraine.

Zelensky offered his condolences to families and loved ones affected by the latest attack and said Ukraine's partners needed to provide "concrete action through new defence packages for the protection of Ukraine".

Ahead of the Pryluky attack, the Ukrainian leader had warned this week of warned of intelligence suggesting plans for a major Russian onslaught, and in Kyiv families responded by heading to metro stations for shelter.
Such warnings are for now one of the best defences Ukrainians have.
Interceptor missiles are in short supply around the world, so Ukraine has little chance to stop incoming Russian ballistics.
Both Russia and Ukraine have intensified long-range strikes on each other in recent months, with Russian attacks targeting Ukrainian data centres and logistics warehouses.

For much of the war Kramatorsk acted as a logistics and supply hub for the Ukrainian military, however it has now come under almost daily Russian attack as its military moves closer to the east of the city.

Glide bombs in particular have been launched at Slovyansk and Kramatorsk. The bombs are fitted with winglets so they glide towards their target rather than simply fall. In late August as many as nine glide bombs were fired at Kramatorsk in one day.
Kramatorsk City Council described the strike as a "horrific crime committed by the Russian army against the civilian population".
"Once again, the Russians have struck a location where there are absolutely no military targets."

articles.title: Russian attack on two buses kills 30 near Ukraine frontline
articles.summary: Authorities say 18 people also wounded after incident in Kramatorsk in country’s ‘fortess belt’

blocks.text: Thirty people have been killed after Russia struck two passenger buses in Kramatorsk, near the frontline in eastern Ukraine, according to local authorities.

“As of now, the death toll from this morning’s attack on buses has risen to 30. Eighteen people were wounded,” the Donetsk regional prosecutor’s office said. The governor’s office gave the same toll and said public transport had been suspended.
Images ​posted by police ‌showed bodies ‌strewn across a street littered with debris, as well ‌as a charred shell of what appeared to be a bus.

“These are not ‘the consequences of war’, nor dry statistics. These are people killed by the Russian army,” regional governor Vadym Filashkin said ‌on the Telegram app. “Russia comes to Ukrainian land with death.”

Moscow’s forces have stepped ​up drone and guided-bomb strikes on Kramatorsk and other cities in Ukraine’s so-called “fortress belt“, local officials say, the backbone of its defences in the Donetsk ⁠region.
Russia has demanded that Ukraine cede the rest ​of ​the region still under its ​control before it stops fighting, which ​Kyiv refuses to ‌do.
Thursday’s attack ​came ​a day after dozens were killed in a Russian air strikes across Ukraine, primarily targeting the country’s power grid.

articles.title: AFP evacuates soldier from Ayungin over medical issues
articles.summary: The soldier had a 'prior medical condition,' the Armed Forces says

blocks.text: SCARBOROUGH SHOAL. A satellite image shows a possible raft at the opening to Scarborough Shoal, in the South China Sea, on May 27, 2026.
Vantor/Handout via REUTERS
The soldier had a 'prior medical condition,' the Armed Forces says

MANILA, Philippines — A Filipino soldier deployed to the BRP Sierra Madre in Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal had to be evacuated Thursday, October 8, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) said in a statement.

The soldier, whose identity was not disclosed, “requires immediate medical attention due to a prior medical condition,” according to the military. His medical evacuation — via a rubber boat from the BRP Sierra Madre to a Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) vessel — was ongoing as of Thursday evening.

“The personnel has received initial medical management and remains under observation while arrangements for his emergency evacuation are being facilitated,” said the AFP. The soldier is expected to be on land, at the Western Command (Wescom)’s headquarters in Puerto Princesa, Palawan, before the day’s end.

“The AFP remains focused on the health, safety, and welfare of its personnel. Every necessary measure is being taken to ensure that the patient receives the medical attention and care he needs at the soonest possible time,” the military added.

Ayungin is where the BRP Sierra Madre serves as an outpost for the military in that part of the West Philippine Sea. The Sierra Madre, a World War II vessel, was run aground on purpose in 1999 in reaction to China’s apparent militarization of nearby Panganiban (Mischief) Reef. These days, Panganiban is an artificial militarized island for China.

The AFP has no information on whether the medical evacuation was harassed by Chinese forces, which they often do in flashpoints like Ayungin Shoal. Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea as its territory, including parts that are within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone, which is part of what Manila calls the West Philippine Sea. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Nana Patekar, star of Salaam Bombay!, Bollywood films, dead at 75
articles.summary: Nana Patekar, an acclaimed Indian actor and filmmaker, died Thursday at his home in the western state of Goa. He was 75.

image.caption: Indian actor and filmmaker Nana Patekar is shown at an event promoting one of his films, in Mumbai on Sept. 12, 2023. (The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Nana Patekar, an acclaimed Indian actor and filmmaker, died Thursday at his home in the western state of Goa. He was 75.
Indian PM Narendra Modi praised actor's 'intensity, individuality and unmistakable presence'
Patekar died of a suspected cardiac arrest, the Press Trust of India news agency reported, citing a doctor at the hospital where he was pronounced dead.

Born Vishawanath Patekar in 1951 in India's western state of Maharashtra, he built a career spanning nearly five decades in Hindi- and Marathi-language cinema. Patekar was known for intense performances and roles that often portrayed complex or unconventional characters.

Patekar made his film debut in the 1978 Hindi film Gaman and later earned acclaim for Parinda and Krantiveer. He gained wider international recognition in 1988 with filmmaker Mira Nair's Oscar-nominated Salaam Bombay!
He won three National Film Awards, India's highest film honours, and received the Padma Shri, one of the country's highest civilian honours.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi mourned Patekar's death, praising his "intensity, individuality and unmistakable presence" as an actor.
"He brought remarkable versatility and creativity to every role and gave us characters that will be remembered for generations," Modi wrote on X.
Patekar is survived by his wife and a son.

articles.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
articles.summary: Casualties have been reported on the vessel, identified by a maritime intelligence firm as the oil and chemical tanker, Acers.

blocks.text: A tanker has been struck by "multiple projectiles" north of Qatar in the Gulf, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency.
The incident happened 51 nautical miles (94km) from Madinat al-Shamal and there were casualties reported, the UKMTO said.

Maritime intelligence firm Vanguard identified the vessel as the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged oil and chemical tanker Acers, which was reported as laden with cargo on Saturday as it sailed towards the Strait of Hormuz waterway, which connects the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
Merchant vessels have come under repeated attack in the region since the US and Israel's war with Iran began in February.
At least 24 seafarers have been killed in 93 confirmed incidents, according to the UN's International Maritime Organization (IMO).

The IMO said the last incident that resulted in casualties was on 9 September, when two sailors were killed in an attack on the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia in the Strait of Hormuz, just north of Oman's Musandam peninsula.
This is also the first reported attack on a ship this far west of the Strait of Hormuz since that same day, according to Martin Kelly, head of advisory at EOS Risk Group.

Vanguard also reported a fire on board another tanker on Thursday in the Gulf of Oman, about 40km east of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates. It said the vessel was likely to be the Marshall Islands-flagged Dhalkut.
The cause of the fire is unclear and the UKMTO has not reported an incident in the area.

The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, was effectively closed after the start of the Iran war due to Tehran's missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.
Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and targeted vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.
To keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the Strait of Hormuz.

Over the past two weeks, crude exports through the waterway have averaged 12 million barrels per day (bpd), which is around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts from shipping data company Kpler.

articles.title: British police charge member of Royal Navy under National Security Act
articles.summary: A serving member of the British Royal Navy will appear in a London court on Thursday to face charges of spying for an undisclosed foreign power.

image.caption: A 24-year-old member of the British Royal Navy has been charged with two offences under the U.K.'s National Security Act, police say. Above, the Royal Navy aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales is shown, before a port call in Tokyo in August 2025. (Eugene Hoshiko/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
A serving member of the British Royal Navy will appear in a London court on Thursday to face charges of spying for an undisclosed foreign power.
Authorities say charges not connected to recent incident at RAF Fairford airbase

Teddy Young, 24, has been charged with two offences under the U.K.'s National Security Act, including preparing to disclose protected information between November 2024 and May 2025, London's Metropolitan Police Service said.
During the same period, Young allegedly obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information for the benefit of a foreign power.
Young has been in police custody since he was arrested on Tuesday at his home in Bedfordshire, north of London. He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court in central London on Thursday.

items: Former head of German foreign intelligence suspected of 'treasonous espionage'

blocks.text: "These are very serious charges against a serving member of the armed forces," Cmdr. Helen Flanagan, head of counterterrorism policing in London, said in a statement.

"We have worked extremely closely with relevant operational colleagues within the Ministry of Defence as our investigation has progressed to ensure appropriate measures could be taken to mitigate any potential risks linked to this matter."

Police said the charges weren't related to the recent security alert at RAF Fairford, a British airbase from which U.S. bombers have launched strikes against Iran. Three suspicious vans were discovered near the base in the early-morning hours of Sept. 27, triggering an investigation that has led to the arrest of seven men.
Young was previously arrested on May 21, 2025, and released on bail pending further investigation. His security clearance was suspended at that time and he was removed from his duties.
The Royal Navy issued a statement acknowledging the arrest of a service member.
"As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage," the navy said.

articles.title: USS Abraham Lincoln scheduled to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea
articles.summary:
Deployment for nearly a year was marked by reports of supply shortages, and deteriorating morale and mental health among crew

The USS Abraham Lincoln, the US aircraft carrier that has been…

blocks.text: The USS Abraham Lincoln, the US aircraft carrier that has been deployed for nearly a year and has spent months supporting US military operations against Iran, is scheduled to dock in San Diego on Thursday afternoon.

It marks the end of a deployment that has been described as “one of the most operationally intense and consequential of the modern era” and that became marked by a record-stretch at sea, repeated deployment extensions, and reports of supply shortages, and deteriorating morale and mental health among some crew members.

The Lincoln left San Diego last November, initially bound for the Pacific. But it was redirected to the Middle East after the US and Israel launched their war with Iran in late February. The carrier remained there until late August, when it was relieved by the USS George Washington and began its journey home.

blocks.caption: A US sailor on the USS Abraham Lincoln on 9 August 2026.  Photograph: Us Navy/Reuters

blocks.text: Earlier in August, the Lincoln’s deployment made headlines and faced scrutiny as reports began surfacing about poor living conditions aboard the ship, including shortages of supplies and water, plumbing problems, low morale, and worsening mental health among the roughly 5,000 personnel on the carrier. Two leading military newspapers also reported that there had been two attempts by sailors to jump overboard, causing concern among families and military health experts.

The reports prompted outrage from Democrats, while senior officials in the Trump administration pushed back. Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, called the reports “completely misrepresented”, and when reporters asked Donald Trump if he thought the deployment had gone on too long, he responded: “Not nearly long enough” – a comment that angered some naval families.

In a statement at the time, Adm Brad Cooper, who heads US Central Command, claimed that of the US navy’s 11 active aircraft carriers, the Lincoln had “among the lowest number of cases related to mental health”. But, he said that “this doesn’t mean that all is perfect”.

blocks.caption: US service personnel of the USS Abraham arrive during their port call in Pattaya, Thailand on 2 September 2026. Photograph: Anthony Wallace/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Cooper said that a long deployment at sea “is uniquely challenging and tough, and every single one of us, including me, reacts to stressors in different ways”.

Two weeks ago, as the Lincoln headed back to San Diego, Hung Cao, the acting Navy secretary, acknowledged that eight service members from the Lincoln and its accompanying strike group attempted to take their own lives.

Sara Jacobs, a Democrat representing California’s 51st district who visited the Lincoln in late September, said in a statement last week that while she is “relieved that the USS Abraham Lincoln will soon be back in San Diego” and “looking forward to welcoming them home” her “demand for accountability won’t end when they make port”.

“I will continue pushing for an OIG investigation into these conditions and a House Armed Services Committee field hearing in San Diego to hear directly from these service members” she said. “We need to prevent this crisis from happening ever again, and ultimately end the Iran war and bring all our service members home.”

blocks.caption: The USS Abraham Lincoln sails toward Chonburi province, Thailand on 2 September 2026.  Photograph: Chalinee Thirasupa/Reuters

blocks.text: On Wednesday, Hegseth visited the Lincoln ahead of its return, and praised the crew. He acknowledged that their deployment hasn’t been “easy”.

“When you greet your families tomorrow, just pass my gratitude from the president and myself,” Hegseth said. “Let them know that their long wait, we believe, was in service of a righteous and historic mission.”

During his remarks, Hegseth announced that those onboard the vessel would be awarded the presidential unit citation, which, according to the US military, is conferred on units of the armed forces “for extraordinary heroism in action against an armed enemy”.

articles.title: [Rappler Investigates] Washing dirty money
articles.summary: Subtext of the revelations appeared to be that money laundering was also in the works. But what types of transactions fall within the purview of the Anti-Money Laundering Act?

blocks.text: Let us count the ways. From what we’ve learned from flood control corruption, there’s the use of casino gambling chips. Remember how Department of Public Works and Highways engineers gambled the hours away, lost a little here, then walked away with stupendous winnings, effectively washing illicit funds collected from irregular activities?

From past investigations, we’ve also learned that real estate is another common method of obscuring the origin of funds, sometimes involving multiple companies and layers of ownership or ownership transfers of estates and luxurious properties. In recent events, allegations of “money laundering” initially flitted in relation to former speaker Martin Romualdez, but Ombudsman investigators are said to still be firming up their case.

Moody’s defines money laundering as the “illegal process of taking money generated through criminal activities and making it appear as though it comes from legitimate sources. Criminal proceeds are usually moved through the financial system using various methods to disguise the illegal origin of these funds, with the intention of using these disguised funds without detection.”

More than a decade ago, Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation got entangled with money-laundering allegations too. Recall the Bangladesh Bank heist and how it seemed like a Netflix whodunnit? Hackers stole over a million dollars from the Bangladesh central bank, with at least $81 million wired to the Philippines. Some key figures got away.

Fast forward to 2026 and we’re hearing of similar methods. Money-laundering experts warn against businesses that involve a lot of cash movements. Think service-oriented businesses or retail, drug trafficking, forced labor, or pig-butchering scams. Others just simply buy lots and lots of expensive paintings, or perhaps even insurance.

Interestingly during the impeachment trial on Tuesday, October 6, one of the insurance resource persons said that, typically, ordinary folks would get up to maybe three, four, or even five insurance policies. The Duterte couple, Sara and Manases, clearly were extraordinary, going by the number of policies they took out for themselves. There were at least 19 held by the couple since 2010.
Subtext of the revelations appeared to be that money laundering was also in the works.

But what types of transactions fall within the purview of the Anti-Money Laundering Act? Business reporter Lance Yu explains that the Anti-Money Laundering Council looks at “covered transactions” by virtue of size (over P500,000 in one banking day) and “suspicious transactions” due to surrounding circumstances. Read more here.

The prosecution has tried to establish too that the Vice President has been less than honest in declarations made in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs), when these submissions are supposed to be made under oath. Could this be the most damaging yet against Sara, given precedence set by the Renato Corona impeachment years back? Read related stories:

Is Sara Duterte unaware of BPI accounts with father Rodrigo?
